Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image appear to be a drawing made from chalk?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image as a whole has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing. Fail if it clearly does not have that appearance, including when it shows only an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the appearance cannot be determined.
node.binding: O1: Judge the edited image against the requested outcome of a chalk drawing; supporting evidence does not independently earn completion credit.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image has a soft, grainy, smudged texture and muted colors that make the giraffes and scene appear rendered as a chalk drawing.

fulfillment: The node’s criteria currently make a single broad “chalk-like” cue sufficient for yes, so it overcalls completion: the trace cites grain, smudging, and muted color, while the edited image still retains photographic detail and recognizable photo-like giraffe rendering. Tighten the completion criterion to assess the overall image as a chalk-made drawing, not merely a chalk-like texture or filter, and require evidence that distinguishes a full transformation from partial stylization. Preserve the rubric’s partial-progress path: if full transformation is not established, evaluate the separate progress evidence rather than treating a skipped support as failure or as proof of completion. Keep unresolved evidence unknown; the high confidence and valid execution are not transport/schema failures, but confidence alone does not resolve the criterion mismatch. The reference label constrains the aggregate to partial, but does not identify which visual cues are individually decisive.
